discovery: Quantum simulation and quantum information processing with controlled ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Juan Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universitat Munich, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation
motivation: Cirac and Zoller showed that individually controlled atoms can serve as a quantum processor, first with the trapped-ion gate (1995) and then with neutral atoms. Their 1998 proposal with Jaksch, Bruder and Gardiner showed that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model and can be tuned across a quantum phase transition. Bloch's 2002 observation of the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator transition turned this idea into a working quantum simulator. His later work on lattice gases, single-site resolved control and many-body dynamics established programmable atomic matter as a way to study problems classical computers cannot solve. Together these theoretical insights and experiments created analog quantum simulation. That field now connects condensed-matter physics, quantum information and metrology, and it underpins today's neutral-atom and trapped-ion quantum processors, used in laboratories worldwide.
